status: interpretive mathematical model; not a theorem of physics, psychology, economics or theology

typeCorrection.warning: treating all three as scalar objectives creates an artificial optimization conflict

minimalDynamics.boundaryCondition: at r=r_min require r_dot>=0, hence k<=y-m
minimalDynamics.interpretation: surplus reserve permits a larger temporary outward flow while the boundary rule preserves recoverability

identityLayer.condition: the trajectory must remain inside a declared integrity set I
identityLayer.role: identity is tested by preserved commitments and relations across transformation, not by remaining unchanged

dynamicConsequences: security pursued without an upper stopping rule can displace the life it protects
kenosis without a viability condition can destroy future capacity to serve
selfhood treated as immobility prevents learning and transformation
investment in reserve can enlarge later kenotic capacity
outward contribution can create relational resources and alter the future admissible set
family makes viability a coupled-system constraint rather than an individual preference

illustrativeCheckpoint.interpretation: the interior permits a finite pulse whose continuation eventually tightens as reserve approaches the boundary

conclusion: A good trajectory need not maximize sacrifice, identity expression or wealth. It preserves viability and integrity while permitting the greatest context-appropriate outward flow over time.
